correctness.rationale: In characteristic two the square is a derivation, so checking x,y suffices. Leibniz gives D(xy)=v₁y+v₂x+tr(B)xy and the three displayed coefficient equations. For v≠0, B=uλ_v, c=(λ_v u)u; division by v₁ or v₂ on the corresponding chart gives a regular inverse. For v=0 the equations are B²=0 and Bc=0. For B₀=αwλ_w and c₀=βw, v=tw and u=αw/t+b with λ_w b=β/α yield exactly the polynomial limits stated in the proof. For B₀=0 and c₀≠0 the t² scaling of v and t⁻¹ scaling of u keep c equal to c₀ and specialize B to zero. These curves over an algebraic closure exhaust the boundary of the dense chart. A nonzero v gives two independent images and rank two; at zero v the nonzero block [B|c] has rank one, or all coefficients vanish. A nonzero nilpotent B is specified by its image/kernel line and a nonzero quotient-to-line map, giving q²−1 possibilities and q choices of c; B=0 gives q² choices. The independent direct composition/image-size enumeration gives rank counts (1,9,12) and (1,75,240) over F₂ and F₄.
residual_risks: Only the reduced variety and ordinary endomorphism rank are audited; no statement about radicality of the square ideal or about the full nilpotent scheme.

evidence: The orthogonal-pair model supplies the nonzero locus as the image of the rank-two annihilator bundle over u≠0 with the zero section removed. On v₀≠0, normalize v₀=1 using the scaling ambiguity; then the first column is u and u₀ is determined by u₁,u₂,v₁,v₂.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The bundle is geometrically irreducible; scalar multiplication specializes a nonzero matrix to zero. In the chart (u₁,u₂)≠(0,0) and v₁,v₂ are free, with regular inverses on u₁≠0 or u₂≠0. Thus the matrix presentation mechanically gives precisely the open product, dimension four and rationality even though the chart is not displayed in its abstract.
